title: Beyond WCAG: non-WCAG accessibility considerations
note: Review prompts outside WCAG conformance. These are not ACR terms, not OpenACR values and not findings. Each item needs evidence and human review.

items.title: EN 301 549 user preferences
items.why: EN 301 549 clause 11.7 addresses respecting user preferences. On the web this overlaps with theme and user-agent behavior: contrast, text size, colours, spacing and motion preferences should not be overridden by the product.
items.reference: ETSI EN 301 549 V3.2.1, clause 11.7 (software); web behavior is also an accessibility best practice
items.what_to_collect: Theme/configuration audit for font size, contrast, colours, spacing, forced colours and persistence of user choices.

items.title: Visually induced motion sickness
items.why: Parallax, large transitions, zooming and camera-like movement can make people dizzy or nauseated. WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions is Level AAA and does not cover every motion source at AA.
items.reference: WCAG 2.3.3 is related but not a complete AA test for visually induced motion sickness
items.what_to_collect: Inventory of core/theme animations and transitions; test with motion sensitivity and reduced-motion preferences.

items.title: Reduced-motion preference
items.why: Honouring prefers-reduced-motion is a practical way to reduce motion-triggered discomfort. It is not a standalone WCAG 2.2 AA success criterion.
items.reference: CSS prefers-reduced-motion; WCAG 2.3.3 is related AAA guidance
items.what_to_collect: Check whether core/theme animations respect the preference and whether a non-motion path exists.

items.title: Forced-colors and high-contrast modes
items.why: Windows forced-colors and high-contrast modes must not make controls, focus or status information disappear. This is broader than a single WCAG AA criterion.
items.reference: CSS forced-colors / forced-color-adjust; WCAG 1.4.1/1.4.11 are related
items.what_to_collect: Test core/admin controls, focus indicators, icons and status messages in forced-colors mode.
